name: Artesunate
route_note: IV or IM injection at 0, 12 and 24 h then daily for severe malaria; rectal capsules as pre-referral treatment; oral tablets in combinations
originator: Guilin Pharmaceutical Factory, China (Liu Xu and colleagues)
owner: generic (many); Guilin Pharmaceutical (Fosun Pharma) leading supplier; Amivas in the US

discovery.by: Liu Xu and colleagues, Guilin Pharmaceutical Factory
discovery.note: Hemisuccinate ester of dihydroartemisinin made to give a water-soluble artemisinin for injection.

tagline: Injectable artemisinin that cut deaths from severe malaria compared with quinine
summary: Artesunate is a water-soluble semi-synthetic derivative of artemisinin that can be given intravenously, intramuscularly, rectally or by mouth. Two large trials showed it reduces death from severe malaria by about a third in Asian adults and about a fifth in African children compared with quinine, making it the WHO-recommended treatment for severe malaria. It is also a component of oral combinations such as artesunate/amodiaquine and artesunate/mefloquine.
mechanism: Artemisinins contain an endoperoxide bridge that is activated by ferrous iron and haem released when the parasite digests haemoglobin. Activation generates carbon-centred free radicals that alkylate haem and many parasite proteins, causing widespread damage and very rapid killing of blood-stage parasites, including young ring stages.

Artesunate is rapidly hydrolysed to dihydroartemisinin, the main active metabolite. By killing circulating ring-stage parasites before they mature and sequester in small blood vessels, it limits the microvascular damage behind severe malaria. Dead infected cells are removed by the spleen ('pitting'), which can be followed by delayed haemolysis.
uses: Initial treatment of severe malaria in adults and children (IV or IM)
Pre-referral treatment of severe malaria in young children (rectal)
Uncomplicated malaria as part of oral ACTs (with amodiaquine, mefloquine, pyronaridine or sulfadoxine–pyrimethamine)

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Artesunate is synthesised at Guilin Pharmaceutical Factory in China.

history.title: SEAQUAMAT
history.detail: In Asian patients, mainly adults, artesunate reduces mortality from severe malaria by about 35% compared with quinine (Lancet).

history.title: WHO guideline
history.detail: WHO recommends IV artesunate for severe malaria in adults in low-transmission areas.

history.title: AQUAMAT and prequalification
history.detail: In African children, artesunate reduces mortality by about 22% compared with quinine; Guilin's injectable artesunate becomes the first WHO-prequalified version.

history.title: Preferred for all
history.detail: WHO recommends parenteral artesunate as first-line treatment for severe malaria in all age groups.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves artesunate for injection (Amivas) in May 2020, replacing quinidine, which had been the only US option.

history.title: Rectal artesunate warning
history.detail: WHO advises that rectal artesunate be used only as part of a full referral pathway after a multi-country study found poor outcomes without follow-on care.

pk.half_life: artesunate under 15 min; dihydroartemisinin about 0.5–1 h
pk.bioavailability: IM well absorbed; oral and rectal variable
pk.metabolism: esterase hydrolysis to dihydroartemisinin, then glucuronidation (UGT1A9, UGT2B7)

serious: post-artesunate delayed haemolysis (1–4 weeks after treatment)

facts: Because it is water-soluble, artesunate is the only artemisinin suitable for intravenous use.
The US approval in 2020 ended reliance on IV quinidine, which had become hard to obtain.
